name: congestion pricing

b1

b3

The Value Pricing Pilot Program agreement between New York State and the federal government authorized New York's congestion pricing tolls.
The Trump administration's effort to end congestion pricing represents an attempt to override New York State's self-governance.
The Trump administration's threat to withhold federal funding was designed to pressure New York State to end the congestion pricing program.
Congestion pricing opponents will continue to challenge the program through legal and political channels.
It is wrong to restrict access to Manhattan based on a driver's ability to pay a toll.
The federal government should not unilaterally terminate a congestion pricing program approved through state and federal processes.
The Metropolitan Transportation Authority filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration's Department of Transportation to challenge the termination of congestion pricing.
New York City's congestion pricing toll charges passenger vehicles $9 to enter Manhattan below 60th Street during peak hours.
The Trump administration's February 2025 letter required New York to cease its congestion pricing tolling operations.

The Trump administration's attempt to terminate congestion pricing contributed to a protracted legal battle that lasted over a year.
The congestion pricing program will generate significant revenue for the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.
